what: whether a UNION of separately-driven section trajectories is the same thing as a COUPLED trajectory at the summed scope. It is not, and the difference decides what the TRAJECTORY clause can honestly ask for.
why_this_was_tested: this row's own plan was to drive aux_heads and msa_module as separate trajectories and report 88.0819 + 2.8431 + 1.2317 = 92.1567 % as the scope reached. That addition is only sound if the three runs compose into one trajectory at 92.1567 %. They do not, and nothing in the campaign's record said so, because until this row only one section had ever been driven as a trajectory and a sum of one term is a coupled scope by accident.

the_mechanism.each_capture_is_frozen: every boundary is a capture of upstream's own r = 0 step. A section driven from it reads THOSE inputs at every one of the 20 steps.
the_mechanism.the_inputs_are_other_sections_outputs: boundary_aux_heads.pt's kwargs are batch, si_input and output.{si_trunk, zij_trunk, atom_positions_predicted}. si_trunk and zij_trunk are the TRUNK's outputs and atom_positions_predicted is the DIFFUSION module's. So at step k an aux_heads trajectory reads upstream's step-0 trunk and diffusion outputs, not our step-k ones.
the_mechanism.what_that_omits: in a real training step the sections are in series: an error in the trunk's update moves the diffusion module's inputs, which moves aux_heads' inputs. A union of frozen-boundary trajectories tests each section's update rule in isolation and tests NONE of that coupling. It is strictly weaker than a coupled trajectory at the same scope, and the two are indistinguishable in a `pct_of_model_sq_grad_norm` field.
the_mechanism.the_diffusion_rung_is_NOT_affected: 88.0819 % is a single COUPLED trajectory. Its scope is one boundary and, on our side, OF3DiffusionConditioning feeding OF3DiffusionModule -- two classes composed in one taped forward, so conditioning's step-k weights are what the transformer's step-k forward reads. The coupling inside the scope is included; only coupling ACROSS captures is not.

capture_inventory.driven_as_a_trajectory: yes -- perf/of3t_trajwiden/traj_widen_shipped.json, 20 steps, 88.0819 % reached of the 89.2106 % spanned
no; and 0.74055 of its 0.8007 is host-applied, so no device gradient exists for it at all

the_bound_this_puts_on_a_coupled_traject.so: 88.0819 % is not merely this row's result. It is within 1.13 points of the MAXIMUM coupled trajectory scope available from any capture the campaign holds, because the diffusion boundary is the widest-spanning one and we already reach 98.74 % of what it spans. Every route past it needs a capture that spans more than one section.

the_whole_model_route.reference_side: DRIVABLE, and this contradicts SCOPE_LADDER.json's note that 'a taped whole-model forward needs a full featurised batch and this row's capture is a diffusion boundary, not a batch'. True of that row's capture; the BUNDLE has the batch. of3t-campaign-refs/bundle_min_043 holds batch_step003.pt (100,822,382 B, sha256 3c32597a20f09bf5..., 5nw3, 56 tokens), w0_043.pt (4,573,746,297 B) and draws_recycles0.pt (525,598 B), all digest-pinned in MANIFEST.json. Upstream's OF3AllAtom in float64 over that batch with the replayed draws is a whole-model reference step.
the_whole_model_route.device_side: NOT AVAILABLE. There is no taped whole-model forward+backward on our side. perf/of3t_gradients/instrument_full_model.py builds the shipped model on a card and PLACES upstream's tensors onto ours by exact bf16 value; its own docstring says what it 'deliberately does NOT do: compare a gradient MAGNITUDE'. It is a mapping instrument, not a gradient one. The campaign's 92.1568 % model-scope reading (MODEL_d56_retake.json) is assembled as a UNION of four separately-driven arms for exactly this reason.
the_whole_model_route.so_the_blocker_is_named: reaching a coupled trajectory scope above 89.2106 % requires building a taped whole-model device forward+backward. That is porting work with a known cost shape, not a measurement, and it is a different thing from the 1.2744 % that has no device gradient at any scope.

what_this_does_to_the_proposed_clause.the_problem: PROPOSED_CLAUSE.md proposes `scope.pct_of_model_sq_grad_norm >= 97.9849`. That number was built by ADDING section shares whose device gradient arms exist. A union of frozen-boundary trajectories can satisfy it while testing no cross-section coupling at all, which is the D181 failure mode in a new place: the clause reads a scope, and the instrument that reaches it is a union of decoupled runs.
what_this_does_to_the_proposed_clause.the_repair: the clause must say which KIND of scope it reads. Two numbers, not one: a COUPLED scope, which is bounded at 89.2106 % by the widest capture and sits at 88.0819 % today, and a UNION scope, which is bounded at 92.1568 % by the device arms that exist. Reporting one number for both is what lets a weaker instrument pass.
what_this_does_to_the_proposed_clause.recommendation: TRAJECTORY should read the COUPLED scope, because the thing it exists to prove -- that the gradient the model produced reached the optimizer and that step k+1's forward read the weights step k wrote -- is a statement about a composed forward. A union tests it once per section and never across them.
